newsitem.title: USA: Foster Wheeler to appeal incinerator ruling.
newsitem.headline: Foster Wheeler to appeal incinerator ruling.

text.p: Foster Wheeler Corp will appeal an Illinois judge's ruling last week dismissing its legal challenge to the repeal of a state subsidy for waste-to-energy incinerators, senior vice president and general counsel Thomas O'Brien said Tuesday.
Foster Wheeler "obviously" disagrees with the Cook County Circuit Court judge's decision and will file an appeal "expeditiously" with the Illinois Appellate Court, O'Brien said.

The developer of a partly bond-financed incinerator in the village of Robbins south of Chicago, Foster Wheeler contends that the Illinois General Assembly's partial repeal of the Retail Rate law in 1996 was improper and unconstitutional, O'Brien said.

Judge Robert Boharic on Friday held that the lawsuit and challenges filed by developers of incinerators in Ford Heights and Fulton sought to impose liability on the state and therefore could be brought only in the Illinois Court of Claims.
"As I understand it, the Court of Claims has no power to decide constitutional issues," O'Brien said.

Foster Wheeler, CGE Ford Heights and CGE Fulton had developed incinerators based on the state subsidy that allowed them to charge public utilities a higher rate for the electricity they generated in the waste-to-energy facilities.
The incinerator in Robbins was completed, has operated on a temporary construction permit and is currently shutdown while awaiting a permanent operating license due to issue on June 2, O'Brien said.
Developers moth-balled the already completed Ford Heights facility when lawmakers repealed the subsidy.
Chicago attorney Philip Beck, who represents CGE Ford Heights, said he had not completed reviewing Boharic's ruling on Tuesday and declined to comment on the decision.

The Ford Heights facility was partly financed by $79.5 million of tax-exempt bonds sold through the Illinois Development Finance Authority, Robbins with $320 million of bonds and the yet-to-be-built facility in Fulton with $84.6 million of bonds.
CGE Ford Heights filed for bankruptcy in 1996 and under an agreement with bondholders will continue to make interest payments only until Oct. 1.
A separate challenge to the repeal, filed by Polsky Energy Corp., remains pending in another state jurisdiction. An appeal taken from the dismissal of a federal lawsuit also remains pending.
Supporters of the incinerators have made several attempts to reinstate the subsidy in some form during the current legislative session.
